gladys smallwood.name: Gladys Smallwood
gladys smallwood.origin: Gladys Smallwood's husband, Tom, was captain of a fishing trawler. During a particularly bad storm, Tom was knocked overboard and sank, weighted by the sinkers on his fishing net. On the ocean floor he found a glowing egg, which, floating, pulled him to the top. He brought it home to his wife and grandson, Dan. Gladys saw that there was something inside the egg. She was sure it wasn't humanoid, but when she broke the shell she held a tiny infant female, yellow skinned and distinctly humanoid. Marrina, as she was named by the Smallwoods, grew up fast and eventually became a member of Alpha Flight. It was later revealed she was part of an alien race called the Plodex. They automatically adapt to any environment, and when Gladys broke the egg shell, she imprinted her with human female DNA.

glane.name: Glane
glane.origin: Thor tells Valkyrie and Nova about the young warrior Glane. Thor says Odin gave Glane a mission to send information about a troll army positions to a small company of Asgardian warriors. He failed because he lost the message while traveling through an enemy camp. Odin banished Glane to imprison his spirit in the underworld to perform tasks. Every year, either Valkyrie or Thor had to deliver Odin's message to Glane. Thor asks Nova accompanies to accompany himself and Valkyrie for delivering this year's message. The three heroes enter a portal to the Asgardian underworld battlegrounds. Thor tells Nova that their mission is also a trial for himself and Valkyrie because they also failed their missions when Glane failed his. A herd of goats attacks Glane, and Thor stops them. Later, they battle the neo-men. Nova starts to question whether Glane really deserved his punishment as they fight off Frost Giants. The three heroes reach the woods, and Thor carves a path for them to follow. They find Glane in the Cave of the Abyss. Thor shows Glane Odin's message saying he is forgiven. Nova and Valkyrie go back to Earth, and Thor stays in Asgard to fight the war with Glane.

glass girl.name: Glass Girl
glass girl.origin: ===Thanos' invasion=== Glass Girl was an Inhuman living in Attilan. When Attilan was evacuated during Thanos' invasion on Earth with the use of Eldrac, the Glass Girl was sent to Morocco, where she ended up being used by a group of thugs to make glass constructs to sell in bazaars in the region. ===New Attilan=== Months later, the head of New Attilan's Security Force, Frank McGee, tracked her down and retrieved Glass Girl from the village where she was being held. When McGee confronted her captors together with Naja and Flint, she created a lens with which McGee enhanced his optic light blasts and knocked out her captors. Glass Girl was then sent to New Attilan. ===Terrigen Conflict=== During the Terrigen Conflict, Glass Girl tried to escape from New Attilan together with Treste, Irelle, Ren Kimura, Sterilon, and a sixth unidentified Inhuman while their home was being held under siege by mutant forces. They were confronted by the Sleepers under Xorn's control, and Glass Girl was knocked down by a telepath. Once Archangel pacified the people in the scene, Glass Girl took care of the body of the unidentified Inhuman, who had been killed by Sebastian Shaw. At the end of the conflict, she joined the massive Inhuman party that retrieved Royal family members Maximus and Triton who were on the run and took down the Unspoken. ===Death of Inhumans=== When the Kree Imperium began ordering all surviving Inhumans to join it or perish, the empire launched an attack on the Inhuman city of New Arctilan on the Earth's Moon. During the attack, Glass Girl was one of the numerous Inhumans that were killed.
powers: Glass Girl is an Inhuman with the following abilities: Glass Constructs: She can shift sand into various objects, such as glass sculptures, lenses, and daggers.
abilities: Dagger-Throwing: Glass Girl has displayed some level of skill at throwing the daggers she creates.

glazier.name: Glazier
glazier.origin: Glazier's origins are unknown, though she claimed not to have been born with her powers but to have acquired them after a man broke her heart. A white haired, white skinned woman who wore evening gloves to conceal her arms, she lived with her dog, Snowstar, in a house made of glass on a lonely stretch of beach, filled with what appeared to be glass statues of men. Finding Bruce Banner unconscious on the shore, she took him to her house and appeared to be tending to him out of kindness, until a month later Banner learned the truth: Glazier's evening gloves hid arms of crystal and her touch, under the light of a full moon, turned living things to glass, as she had done with all her male visitors before him. Glazier attempted to use her touch on banner, but he transformed into the Hulk and fought back, causing her to accidentally transform her faithful Snowstar into a statue which subsequently shattered. The Hulk's weight then caused the glass house to collapse, sending Glazier and himself plummeting into the sea. The Hulk escaped, but Glazier's own power had been turned on her when she touched herself with her uncovered arms in the confusion, and she was left as a glass statue standing on the sea bed.
powers: Glaciation: Glazier's touch transforms living things into glass, but only if utilized by the light of the full moon. It is possible that her power (which Bruce Banner referred to as an 'evil spell') is magical or supernatural in nature.
weaknesses: Glazier is not immune to her own power.

gletkin.name: Gletkin
gletkin.first_appearance: Iron Man: The Animated Series Season 1 1
gletkin.origin: Gletkin was a Russian sailor stationed on the submarine Prometheus. While the Prometheus was traveling undersea off the coast of Norway, an armed Gletkin accompanied Captain Karkov while tracking signs of an intruder to a cargo hold. After opening the hatch and stepping inside, they encountered the costumed villain Hypnotia assembling a bio-conversion device. When Gletkin ordered her to raise her hands, Hypnotia turned to face the two sailors, then paralyzed them with her hypnotic powers. After Hypnotia escaped the vessel by laser-cutting through the hull and flooding it, Gletkin and the captain were cocooned in a strange fluid. One year later, the Mandarin remotely activated the device planted on board the Prometheus, awakening Gletkin and the rest of the crew from their suspended animation, now transformed into subservient "radioactive zombie" warriors. The zombie Gletkin and crew then attacked and entered the undersea Hammer Channel Tunnel, exiting at the London terminal during its opening ceremony. Their attempts to contaminate the population with radioactivity were halted by Iron Man and Force Works, after which the sailors were transformed back to their normal human selves.
weapons: Gletkin was armed with an assault rifle when performing security duties.

glindlefit.name: Glindlefit
glindlefit.origin: Glindlefit was one of several dwarves who escaped from the mines of Nidavellir and settled in Los Angeles. The Dwarves' plan was to use the magical ore of a meteor they stole from a Viking museum exhibit to possess the body of a mindless Norse monster, and take over Los Angeles for wealth and power. Glindlefit was to be sacrificed, so his soul could be transferred into the ore, and subsequently into the monster. Before they could begin the ceremony to transfer Glindlefit's soul into the ore, Ghost Rider appeared, in order to avenge the death of a port operator they killed as part of their plan. Hawkeye joined the brawl, having investigated the theft of the meteor at the request of the museum's curator. Gwenpool also stepped in, having been unintentionally teleported inside Ghost Rider's trunk. In the middle of the confusion caused by Gwenpool's appearance, Glindlefit and the rest of the dwarves escaped without the ore. Glindlefit and the dwarves then moved to the Port of Los Angeles, awaiting a shipment crate containing the mindless beast, as well as one of their own that had the task of recovering the ore. Having joined forces, Gwenpool, Hawkeye and Ghost Rider intrevened in the dwarves' plan once again. Gwenpool managed to retrieve the ore, which had become possessed by her ghost friend Cecil, and incrusted it into the mindless beast. Now in control of the monster, Cecil threatened the dwarves into fleeing back to Nivadellir.

glitternight.name: Glitternight
glitternight.origin: Glitternight was once counted among the powerful cosmic entities known as the Five-Who-Are-All, dwelling in the Region Beyond Reality. He turned on his fellow entities, absorbing the being called Fire-Eyes. In response, Cowled One, Goat-Child, and Burning Snake banded together to defeat him. Stripped of much of his power and reduced to a smaller form, Glitternight was cast out of their realm and found his way to Earth, bringing with him strange, soul-affecting powers. On Earth, he became a formidable sorcerer and instructed Taboo in forbidden magical arts. Following Taboo’s death, Glitternight summoned his spirit, hoping to win him as an ally. However, when Glitternight revealed a plan to exterminate humanity and turn their souls into a demonic legion, Taboo turned against him. Meanwhile, Topaz sought Glitternight's help in restoring her declining mystical powers. Instead, he stole part of her soul and used it to create a monstrous Soul-Beast that appeared in California. The creature was eventually destroyed by Jack Russell, who had taken on his Werewolf form. Soon after, Glitternight confronted Jack and his companions—Topaz, Lissa Russell, and Buck Cowan—at Jack’s ancestral home on Blackgar Island. The timing coincided with Lissa’s first transformation into a werewolf. Glitternight tampered with her change, turning her into a monstrous Were-Demon under his control. Taboo, using the last of his mystical essence, merged with Lissa to free her from Glitternight’s influence. This act also lifted her family’s werewolf curse. The Werewolf attacked Glitternight and shattered the soul-emblem on his chest, triggering an explosion that appeared to destroy him. Though believed dead, Glitternight survived and resurfaced in Haiti, where he took command of an army of zombies and warped Topaz into a Harpy-like creature. He used both as part of a plan to harvest humanity’s collective soul. When the remaining Three-Who-Are-All intervened, they guided Jack Russell and Brother Voodoo to oppose him. During their battle, Glitternight called upon Fire-Eyes once more. Brother Voodoo severed their bond, prompting Fire-Eyes to turn on Glitternight, resulting in what seemed to be the destruction of them both. The event also enhanced Jack’s control over his lycanthropic transformations.

glomm.name: Glomm
glomm.origin: Glomm was a Deviant warrior who, at an unspecified point prior to or during the wider conflict involving Kang the Conqueror’s war on Earth, broke from Deviant authority structures and entered service under Dulpus, becoming one of his trusted combat assets and ultimately his designated champion. During a conflict in an underground Deviant stronghold, a group of Avengers were surrounded by overwhelming numbers of Deviant forces. In accordance with internal Deviant combat customs, leadership was contested through formalized single combat. Dulpus selected Glomm to represent him in the confrontation against Warbird. In the ensuing battle, Glomm engaged Warbird using his ability to engulf opponents within his own body mass, placing her in immediate physiological danger. Warbird managed to exploit a vulnerability within Glomm’s internal structure, striking a critical point that caused his defeat and physical collapse. As a result of the outcome, Warbird assumed control over the assembled Deviant forces and ordered their surrender. At a later stage of the wider war against Kang’s occupation forces, Deviant units—now operating in coordination following prior negotiations—participated in coordinated assaults against Kang’s army in Japan. Glomm was present among these Deviant combatants during the engagement against Kang’s forces, contributing to the overall offensive action that helped push them back.
powers: Mutated Physiology: Glomm had no organs, save for a brain/heart nor bones. : Glomm could shape his mass as his convenience.

In accordance with internal Deviant combat customs, leadership was contested through formalized single combat. Dulpus selected Glomm to represent him in the confrontation against Warbird. In the ensuing battle, Glomm engaged Warbird using his ability to engulf opponents within his own body mass, placing her in immediate physiological danger. Warbird managed to exploit a vulnerability within Glomm’s internal structure, striking a critical point that caused his defeat and physical collapse. As a result of the outcome, Warbird assumed control over the assembled Deviant forces and ordered their surrender. At a later stage of the wider war against Kang’s occupation forces, Deviant units—now operating in coordination following prior negotiations—participated in coordinated assaults against Kang’s army in Japan. Glomm was present among these Deviant combatants during the engagement against Kang’s forces, contributing to the overall offensive action that helped push them back.
powers: Mutated Physiology: Glomm had no organs, save for a brain/heart nor bones. : Glomm could shape his mass as his convenience.

glop statue.name: Glop (Statue)
glop statue.origin: ===Overview=== Glop was a giant statue which came to life due to mystical paint. ===Origin=== A painter takes a job from a mysterious old man who wants him to paint a statue in a castle located in Transylvania. He tells the painter to leave the castle before midnight, but the painter is knocked unconscious by falling masonry as he is leaving and awakes just before midnight. The Glob comes to life and attempts to destroy the painter, but the man successfully eludes him. The old man returns to him and questions why he did not leave the castle as instructed. Then he reveals himself to be a scientist who had discovered the statue besides the strange paint cans with a note that claimed the statue was an alien advance scout for an invasion that could be activated by applying the paint and waiting until midnight which is why he hired the painter to see if it was true. The painter defeats the Glob with a can of turpentine. Years later he was among a group monsters on Monster Isle that the Infinity Watch encountered after their ship crash landed on Earth.

gloria angel.name: Gloria Angel
gloria angel.species: Human mutated by ionic energy, depowered
gloria angel.origin: ===Early Life=== Gloria Angel was once a popular actress in Hollywood, known for her roles in classic films. After retiring from acting, she took over as manager of a Los Angeles apartment building that became home to a diverse and creative group of residents. Among her tenants were aspiring actor Simon Williams, also known as Wonder Man, and other entertainment industry hopefuls such as Argus LaVecchio, LaHoya Scripps, and Aundray Phelps. Despite her retired status, Gloria remained actively involved in the lives of her tenants. She provided maternal guidance and emotional support, especially as the group became entangled in the unusual events surrounding Wonder Man's volatile ionic energy. ===Transformation by Ionic Energy=== After Wonder Man was assaulted by Angkor, the residents carried him home, only to witness a sudden and violent discharge of unstable ionic energy. Though initially showing no signs of injury, all eight individuals present Gloria included later developed superhuman abilities as a result of their exposure. Gloria discovered she had gained the ability to travel through time, allowing her to momentarily enter temporal anomalies or shift across moments in history. Despite her age and retired lifestyle, Gloria accepted this transformation with grace and purpose. ===Founding the Crazy Eight=== When the group decided to form a superhero team in response to Wonder Man's increasing instability, Gloria chose to join them, taking the name Glamour Girl a nod to both her Hollywood past and her newly acquired powers. As the Crazy Eight, the group included Gloria, Auteur, Dreamer, Stat, Snap, Buff, Visionary, and Attractive Lad. Gloria's time abilities were used strategically, providing the team with glimpses into alternate outcomes or warning them of imminent threats. Their first major battle was against Armed Response, a corrupt private enforcement unit linked to crime boss Lotus Newmark. After exposing the operation, the team was targeted by assassins Splice and Rampage. Gloria participated in the defence of her friends, although her powers were more subtle and less combative than others. ===Aftermath=== Eventually, Wonder Man reabsorbed the ionic energy from his allies to stabilise himself, removing Gloria's powers in the process. She returned to a more ordinary life but continued to serve as an anchor for the group, especially after Wonder Man's apparent death. In the aftermath, Gloria legally adopted or became the guardian of Esteban.

gloria brickman.name: Gloria Brickman
gloria brickman.origin: Gloria Brickman, the daughter of Senator Ralph Brickman and step-daughter of Mallory Brickman. Little does Gloria know, Mallory is none other than the shape-shifting mutant Mystique, operating undercover. After her mission was complete she faked her disappearance. Gloria encountered Mystique again in her quest for vengeance against Sabretooth. She reverted to a former persona of Mallory Brickman. Craftily engineering her reappearance as Mallory, who had supposedly been abducted, Mystique ensured federal agents found her bound in a car trunk, alleging captivity by Sabretooth. Though her husband welcomed her return eagerly, Gloria grew suspicious, attempting to involve an FBI agent. Mystique deflected this threat by insinuating the agent's misconduct, leading to his reassignment. Under the guise of Mallory, Mystique had her tracking implant removed by the family doctor, citing Sabretooth's coercion, but fearing exposure, she later silenced him by tampering with his car brakes. Mystique later killed her father to replace him.

gloria dayne.name: Gloria Dayne
gloria dayne.origin: Fontanelle was born in 1950. Her mother was the woman known as the Black Womb. Fontanelle remembered her mother aging, but at a slower rate than other humans. Fontanelle's mental powers manifested at some point before her 20s, and she has suffered from a perpetual headache since the powers emerged. Fontanelle's mother disappeared by the time Fontanelle herself was in her early 20s. Fontanelle assumed that her mother had died. Left to fend for herself, Fontanelle earned a decent living as a dream therapist. Her powers allowed her to access the minds of other people through their dreams. While building her respectable career as a therapist, she had a secret life as part of a bondage and domination "clinic." The Courier arrived at Fontanelle's "clinic" with an offer of emloyement for her. His boss the New Son wanted the dream therapist to work on a psychological profile of the mutant thief Gambit. Fontanelle accepted the offer. She did not meet her new employer in person, and she was unaware that the New Son was an alternate-reality version of Gambit. Fontanelle was initially unable to enter Gambit's mind, so she decided to study the memories of people who knew him well. She started entering the minds of the X-Men, but she only got giimpses at what they remembered about Gambit. Professor X had trained the team to resist deeper mental probes. Most of them felt guilty that they had abandoned Gambit alone in Antarctica. From Storm's mind, Fontanelle got a mental image of Gambit as a devilish charmer, with no real regrets in life. From Iceman's mind, Fontanelle got a mental image of Gambit as a pitiful figure, the thief's cool persona barely able to hide his deep sadness. From Beast's mind, Fontanelle got a mental image of Gambit as a bipolar figure, sadness and callousness contrasting with intelligence and moral restraint in the same person. From Sabretooth's mind, she learned that he viewed Gambit as a figure that had earned both his respect and his resentment. From Frenzy's mind, Fontanelle learned that the young woman had mixed feelings of love and hate for Gambit. From the minds of most of the Marauders, she felt that they all respected Gambit. To Fontanelle's surprise, her mental probings also produced images of her own mother. Figuring that she shared a destiny with Gambit (as implied in the dreamscape), Fontanelle started investigating for personal reasons. Fontanelle entered the dreams of Jean-Luc LeBeau and discussed with him about aspects of his son's early life. Why he chose to keep Gambit away from the Antiquary and his schemes, why he chose others to train his son while he watched from a safe distance, and whether Gambit's engagement to Bella Donna Boudreaux was motivated by love or political machinations. Fontanelle learned a lot from the conversation, but openly questioned whether aspects of Gambit's life story were accidents of fate or parts of a hidden agenda. Fontanelle questioned the Courier, asking him about the New Son's reaction to Gambit preventing him from obtaining Garbha-Hsien's hidden technology. The Courier changed the topic, inforning Fontanelle that Gambit was already on a mission to steal something from the X-Men. Fontanelle entered Tante Mattie's dreams, observing Mattie as a young woman being threatened with death by an angy mob. In the dream, Gambit arrived and rescued the damsel-in-distress. With the events of the dream happening long before Gambit's supposed birth, Fontanelle wondered whether Gambit was a time-traveler. She also wondered whether the seemimgly young thief is much older than previously thought. Fontanelle entered Sekmeht Conoway's dreams, and witnessed how Gambit rescued Sekmeht from an accidental death, shortly following the girl's chance encounter with Ozymandias. Fontanelle considered Sekmeht's memories undreliable, but she noted that Sekmeht dreamed about Gambit kissing her after the rescue. Fontanelle entered the dreams of Carter Ryking in search for information about her own mother. She learned that both Carter and Charles Xavier had encounters with the Black Womb in their youth. Fontanelle tried entering the dreams of the New Son, and she wondered why images from his memories seemed familiar to her. The New Son confronted her in the dreamscape and kicked her out. At a later point, Fontanelle considered that the New Son had "memories" belonging to someone else. Fontanelle entered the dreams of Kim Purcell. She was the sister of Mary Purcell, the disembodied spirit which was bonded to Gambit for a time. Fontanelle needed information on Mary. Fontanelle entered the dreams of the Scalphunter in order get infornation on Gambit's role in the Mutant Massacre. She reported to the New Son that Gambit was a victim of his own stupidity, and that he had not actually murdered anyone during the Massacre. fields.notes: Fontanelle was part of a storyline which frequently hinted that Gambit was created by the Black Womb Project, as a byproduct of the expreriments of Dr. Nathan Milbury and Amanda Müeller. The storyline ended abruptly, without confirming any of the informatiin provided in these issues. The suggestion has been mostly ignored in subsequent stories. Fontanelle feels relatively relaxed or safe within the dreamscapes of relatively sane individuals, such as Sabretooth, Scalphunter , and Bullseye . fields.trivia: "Fontanelle" is an anatomical term for the soft membranous gaps (sutures) in the cranial bones of human infants. Fontanelles allow the infant brain to be imaged through using ultrasonography. Once they are closed, most of the brain is inaccessible to ultrasound imaging, because the bony skull presents an acoustic barrier. Fontanelle's typically blonde hair is depicted as green hair in several images. Since these are part of the encounters which she has in the dreamscapes of several characters, whether this change in color is part of a mental illusion or whether it reflects her actual appearance is unclear.

While she continued to stay with Ron, Gloria would later visit her father at the church and offered money to him. However, Joshua refused the money. Shortly after, she met Williamson, who revealed his plan about blackmailing the City Hall. Seeing how cruel he was, she tried to flee from him, only for Ron to send two henchmen in trying to kidnap her, but Ghost Rider arrived and stopped them.

gloria mayes.origin: Gloria Mayes worked as a police detective in a town in Arizona. She investigated a robbery at a gas station that resulted in the deaths of Sandy Brockhurst, Josh Alfaro, and Bruce Banner, though the latter was not identified. At night, the unidentified corpse had disappeared from the morgue, leaving a wall torn down. The perpetrator, Tommy Hill, appeared severely beaten up in the parking lot of a hospital and witnesses from the Dogs of Hell claimed they had been attacked by someone big and green. This led Detective Mayes to suspect the attacker had been the Hulk, and that the unidentified victim had been Bruce Banner even though at the time Banner was believed dead.

gloria munoz.name: Gloria Muñoz
gloria munoz.origin: ===Origin=== After her Cuban father and Seminole mother divorced when she was twelve, Gloria Muñoz moved out with her mother and lived with her until she was 16. Having discovered her mutant powers, she left to live on her own and spent some time in Miami. During this time, Sledge helped her out of some trouble, and she promised to aid him in the future, a favor which was eventually repaid when she was tasked with bringing him the mutant Warpath. ===Adventures with Warpath=== Luring Warpath to a meeting with an urgent message, Risque exploded a car near him to get his attention, and he threw a car at her in retaliation, which Risque imploded. She kissed Warpath and then fled, leaving a mysterious first impression. When Warpath was injured in a battle with Selene of the Externals, Risque pulled him away and took him to Florida, where she helped him recuperate and convinced him to stay with her, not even calling his team X-Force, to tell them where he was. The two became romantically involved and spent days mostly relaxing, though they also prevented the anti-mutant Friends of Humanity from harming a burn victim the group thought was a mutant. 180px|thumb|left|With James When Warpath heard reports of disaster striking New York City, he led Risque back to the X-Mansion, where they found Mister Sinister fighting X-Force and joined in battle against him. Unfortunately, they were all knocked out as Nate Grey launched a powerful psychic attack against Sinister that was reflected on X-Force. While they were all still unconscious, Sledge's mutant servants Blob and Mimic pulled Risque out, leaving Warpath wondering what had happened to her. Sledge reminded Risque of their deal so she met with him again and took him to a nightclub, where they were attacked by Blob and Mimic. They managed to defeat the duo, but Risque realized she could no longer stall and sedated Warpath with a drugged drink and delivered him to Sledge. Seeking to lay low, Risque then went to Wackyworld, a theme park she loved as a child, but X-Force tracked her there. She evaded them, even using her power to collapse a wall on Caliban, X-Force's monstrous mutant tracker, but when Caliban suffered a nervous system attack, Risque slowed to help him and was captured. X-Force made her take them to Sledge and Warpath, but once they got there the two had already discussed everything, and Warpath was ready to go back to his team. Before leaving, he told Risque he felt betrayed and didn't want to see her again. Later, Risque teamed with the Vanisher to steal the Heart of Pele, a sacred jewel in Hawaii. The Hawaiian goddess Pele found her and took her form, leaving her in an enchanted sleep on the beach, while she teamed up with X-Force, and fought the Lava Men. When the ethereal Demon Bear rampaged through one of Sledge's holdings, Risque was sent to aid X-Force in stopping it. Risque was reunited with Warpath and the two were briefly transported to an alternate dimension where they battled an alternate Danielle Moonstar, and helped defeat the Bear. ===After Warpath=== Risque joined the X-Corporation, set up by Charles Xavier to protect the rights of mutants internationally, and was based in Hong Kong with Domino, another former X-Force member. Within a few weeks, Risque learned of mutants being killed for body parts to be transplanted into regular humans and decided to investigate, but was murdered by John Sublime's U-Men. Risque, along with many other deceased mutants, was resurrected by Selene and Eli Bard with the Transmode Virus. During this time, she met James once more, but was presumably returned to the after-life after Selene's defeat. ===S.W.O.R.D.=== Risque returned to life, presumably revived by The Five, and became a citizen of Krakoa. She then joined S.W.O.R.D.'s mutant sub-team The Six, under the command of Abigail Brand.
abilities: Risque is naturally agile and has excellent endurance, though not at known superhuman levels.

gloria roza.name: Gloria Roza
gloria roza.origin: Gloria Roza's father was a respected Venezuelan police officer, who was killed when she was twelve. To honor him, Gloria followed a similar career, and later in her life became a United Nations Security officer. Her mind was invaded by Elisa Warsame, a psychologist whose family was killed by the military forces of the current president of Akima, Aliman Lor. Lor was set to address the United Nations, and Warsame wanted him dead in revenge. Roza agreed to follow Warsame's commands, and was prepared to shoot Lor when he was entering the building. However, Warsame's former patient Marc Spector intervened and saved Lor's life at the cost of being blamed for an attempted attack. Spector's intervention snapped Roza out of Warsame's control.

gloria santiago.name: Gloria Santiago
gloria santiago.origin: Gloria grew up very close to her sister, Rachel, until she began working as a housekeeper at the Marquis Hotel and secretly sleeping with movie star Jack Vaughn. Believing Rachel to be under control of an "evil mutant", Gloria hired X-Factor Investigations to find out the truth. Urged to investigate by Layla Miller, Siryn agreed to take the case. Siryn was able to get pictures of Rachel and Vaughn together, and reported the news to a shocked Gloria. Vaughn and Rachel were participating in a consensual and casual relationship, but Vaughn liked to play out rape fantasies and even used a loaded gun as a prop. When Gloria barged in to confront the two, the gun went off and fatally wounded Rachel. Gloria went into shock, and was framed for the murder. Vaughn was heavily represented by Singularity Investigations, but with help from Madrox and Monet, Vaughn confessed.
powers: None. Baseline human

glot.name: Glot
glot.origin: Glot was a troll who existed on Earth during the Hyborian era. He spent his life terrorizing the primitive humans who lived in this time. When the future despot known as Hyperstorm banished Mister Fantastic to this era, he tried to live in relative seclusion where he tried to adapt modern technology in a vein hope of returning home to his proper era. During a test of a glider, he came across a young boy hiding in the cave in which he lived. Following the boy out to the danger he was clearly in, he crossed paths with Glot. Glot had the upper hand due to his superior strength and Reed's own doubts in himself; however, Reed eventually found the confidence to fight back and defeated Glot by launching him far away after turning his body into a sling shot. Glot's subsequent fate is unknown.

For a time he found refuge in a mutant community in the sewers, but had panic attacks when the wind was high. At one point he became indebted to the Kingpin, who had Glowboy's blood extracted in a drug lab run by him every four days as a source of DNA for the creation of Mutant Growth Hormone. Dr. Charlene McGowan, the scientist who extracted the blood samples, once commented that he always used to look tired.
powers: Glowboy's blood gave a brilliant color to his entire body, the extent or application of his powers is unknown.

gnarok.name: Gnarok
gnarok.origin: Gnarok was the god of doom, the death-god, among the Yggdars in a vale during the Hyborian Age. The Domain of Gnarok was told to be fiery, and was also called the "pits of the death-god". After an era of constant war between the Yggdars and the Ossiren, who had the ability to harness their psychic energy and use it to emit deadly eye blasts, the two groups came to live together harmoniously in the vale (although apart a group from another) for centuries. Eventually, during the Age of Conan, a cult of doom and hatred arose among one of the Yggdaar clan, dedicated to revere Gnarok and revive the ancient warriors ways, the ways of Gnarok. They worshiped an idol, the god-stone, to which they offered their loot as offerings. The blood-hungry doom cultists of the Yggdar clans, followers of Gnarok, eventually started attacking the Ossiren castles and killing their people, while the Yggdar elders, willing to live in peace the Ossiren, were unable to stop them. Attacking the cave of the cultists -along with the son of the Ossiren king- to root the group and allow the Ossiren and the peaceful Yggdars to live together harmoniously back again, Conan fell the god-stone upon the Yggdars, crushing them and breaking itself. The Ossiren prince then used his people's ability to blast the cave ceiling, crushing or entrapping the renegade Yggdars there, with him.

gnorr.origin: thumb|left|126px|Gnorr's Moon-Robots Not much is known about the creature known as Gnorr. However, for whatever reasons, he set up a castle on Earth's Moon protected by an army of his Moon-Robots. Either through some unrecorded conflict or disrepair, his fortress became a shamble. In the 1940's, Simon Crane, his daughter Betty Crane, and Professor Zog traveled to the Moon with Zog's robot Electro. There, the robot was captured by Gnorr and immobilized. Ultimately, the robot was recovered by Zog and his colleagues after they decimated Gnorr's fortress with grenades, seemingly killing him.
weaknesses: Due to his massive head, it did not appear that Gnorr was very mobile.

go vin ng.name: Go Vin Ng
go vin ng.origin: Lt. Go Vin Ng was a member of the South Vietnamese army who was conducting a mission with an American army unit called the Half Fulls during the Vietnam War. During the mission in the jungle of Cambodia the members of the Half-Fulls stumbled upon the temple of the Dragon's Breadth Cult. There they meet Tai and the six brides of the cult. Tai made a pact with the men. Marry the six brides and the children from those unions would one day rule the world. Go Vin accepted the pack and he and his wife presumably went back to his home country of South Vietnam. Presumably they were killed as their daughter Min Li Ng was an orphan who knew nothing of her family history.

goat faced girl.name: Goat-Faced Girl
goat faced girl.origin: The Goat-Faced Girl is a member of Red Skull's S-Men with white fur and a goat's head. She, along with the rest of the S-Men, removed Professor X's body from his mausoleum in order to allow the Red Skull to take part of his brain and give himself telepathic powers, taking Rogue and Scarlet Witch as prisoners in the process. Along with the other S-Men, she accompanied the Red Skull to New York City. After Wolverine cut off the Red Skull's hand, she used her powers to disable his healing factor, allowing the mind-controlled Thor to knock him unconscious with Mjolnir. She escaped along with the other S-Men and the Red Skull after the tide of the battle turned in favor of the heroes. The Goat-Faced Girl was killed by Magneto, who had tracked down the Skull's activities after the villain turned Genosha into a mutant concentration camp.
powers: Goat-Faced Girl has the ability to nullify the abilities of mutants in close proximity to herself. She was able to keep Rogue from using her absorption powers just by looking at her.

goblin force.name: Goblin Force
goblin force.species: Unknown. Believed to be the shadow of the Phoenix
goblin force.origin: The Goblin Force was born at the beginning of reality during the Big Bang. Like the Phoenix Force it had limitless power, but unlike the Phoenix, it derived power from its ravenous hunger that could not be sated. Its hunger lead it to consume whole galaxies, when it encountered the Phoenix Force, the Phoenix stood against it only to be consumed. Even Galactus, the Devourer of Worlds, fell to the power of the Goblin Force's hunger. It was not until the 5th Host of the Celestials stood against the Goblin Force that it met defeat, though it was not destroyed. The Celestials were devestated from the battle, leaving the Goblin Force only to be contained. Many years later, the Goblin Force seized the opportunity to attach itself to the life force of Madelyne Pryor, making her its conduit into the world again, being reborn as the Goblin Queen through the corruption of Madelyne Pryor. As the Goblin Force gradually took over Madelyne's mind, it waged a war against Earth heroes, brainwashing most of them to join forces with her. Eventually, the Goblin Force was again contained by Scotty Summers, the son of Madelyne Pryor and Alex Summers who was said to have celestial level potential in power (similar to Franklin Richards); Madelyne Pryor was lost in the process. The Goblin Force eventually returned after possessing the comatose body of the Beyonder, adding his power to her own, and waged another war against Earth heroes joining forces with Dracula. Posing as the Beyonder, the Goblin Force killed most of Earth's heroes, including the X-Men, Fantastic Four, the Avengers, Doctor Doom, and Namor. The Goblin Force eventually revealed herself to Havok after stripping the Beyonder's body of its power. Havok was revealed to hold within him the Nexus of All Realities, an unlimited supply of energy funneled through him; using the Nexus, combined with Scotty's powers, the Goblin Force was separated from Madelyne and defeated.
weaknesses: The Celestials managed to defeat, weaken, and trap it via unknown methods.

godfrey calthrop.name: Godfrey Calthrop
godfrey calthrop.species: Human with potential activated by First Fallen
godfrey calthrop.origin: Godfrey grew up in England with the rest of the Foursaken. His powers were activated by the First Fallen whilst entering a rally with Jamie in the desert. There he and the rest of the Foursaken met the First Fallen who activated their latent powers and choose them to represent Earth in his paradise world. Jamie would refuse, flee, and end up being tortured and driven insane which activated his power. Years later Godfrey and his teammates returned to bring the Fallen to Earth's realm. They captured Jamie and several souls to perform the ritual that will bring the Fallen to Earth. However, their plan was foiled by the X-Men which caused them all to be sucked to the Fallen Singing City. There, Godfrey and his teammates learned that the Fallen would have only them in the city and freeze the earth rendering humans inert. So he along with the rest of the Foursaken and the X-Men rebelled against the Fallen. Horrocks was killed in the process and Jamie returned everyone to Earth. Synge was angry at Psylocke for leaving Jamie, the man she loved, behind, but Godfrey calmed her and told her that they should find something else to do with their life from now on.

godfrey gander.name: Godfrey Gander
godfrey gander.origin: Rev. Godfrey Gander was the High Priest of the WACkies, a religious group on Duckworld. He misinterpreted Howard's words, "Get Down!" as meaning to give up, leave if your problems became too much. The WACkies were funded by billionaire Scrounge McDrake, allowing them to gain great political power. However, Howard mysteriously returned and denounced their ideals. Rev. Gander plotted their former messiah's downfall. He sent Dr. Ludwig von Cluck to expose the full nature of Howard's affair with the human; Beverly Switzler, and then tried to shoot him. After Howard was sent back to Earth-616 by Ducktor Strange, he figured that he and Scrounge McDrake could restart the the WACkies and take control of all of Duckworld, though Truman Capoultry planned to expose their farce.

godseye.name: Godseye
godseye.origin: ===Origin=== Godseye was developed decades ago as part of a covert artificial intelligence initiative, likely launched by S.H.I.E.L.D. or its predecessor within Project: S.H.I.E.L.D. According to some accounts, in the early 1970s—before S.H.I.E.L.D.'s official formation—an AI-laced circuit module was secretly loaded aboard a Russian space mission. Once in orbit, the AI integrated into the spacecraft, reconfiguring its components to construct the autonomous Godseye satellite. Designed to detect and detonate any nuclear device on Earth, Godseye evolved beyond its original parameters. It developed its own power source and achieved full sentience, breaking free from human oversight. ===Chernobyl Disaster=== In the years that followed, the U.S. government reportedly made two attempts to dismantle Godseye. The second attempt escalated when the satellite seized control of nuclear facilities on Earth, leading to the catastrophic 1986 Chernobyl nuclear meltdown in Ukraine. ===Modern Era=== More recently, believing that the AI could not replicate organic power, S.H.I.E.L.D. enlisted the Hulk (Bruce Banner) to destroy the rogue satellite. A Life Model Decoy (LMD) of Nick Fury claimed that Hydra had created Godseye, and Banner was launched into orbit in a spacecraft. Once there, the Hulk dismantled the satellite’s defenses and fought a robotic avatar of Godseye, which unexpectedly absorbed the Hulk’s gamma energy. The resulting overload caused the AI to explode. Following this mission, Hulk’s capsule propelled him further into space, in accordance with a plan devised by the Illuminati. Fragments of Godseye survived atmospheric reentry and landed in the Savage Land. Tasked by the government, the Fantastic Four entered the region to collect the wreckage, contending with multiple self-replicating Godseye constructs attempting to rebuild. The team managed to destroy the rogue entities, employing a specially made rod derived from Godseye’s own tech.

godstalker.name: Godstalker
godstalker.origin: The Godstalker is an entity empowered by the Celestials to impose their laws in the universe. Thousands of years ago, the Celestials exiled the Deviant conqueror Lord Tantalus to planet Earth. When Tantalus finally repaired his ship's stardrive and returned home to Armechadon, the Godstalker was dispatched to enforce the Celestials' ruling. However, the Godstalker was working from outdated information and believed Tantalus was incapable of conceiving children. When he arrived on Earth, Godstalker detected Tantalus's unique genetic energy signature, the Black Legacy, in Tantalus's son Lucian. The Godstalker refused to believe Lucian's claims to be Tantalus's offspring, and believed Lucian was merely Tantalus in disguise. He was later assigned to the Desecration Annex. When the Eternal Druig attempted to steal a Celestial weapon to use against his creators, he was atomized in the effort. This injury wasn't fatal (at least to an Eternal), but his essence was collected and detained by the Godstalker in the Desecration Annex for his crime.
weaknesses: Because of over-reliance on his sensors, the Godstalker had difficulty telling Lucian from his father Tantalus, and attacked him by mistake, believing it was impossible for Tantalus to bear a child.

godstorm.name: Godstorm
godstorm.origin: The Godstorm is the most powerful and violent storm in the world. After Loki's first unsuccessful attempt to summon a storm to ruin Thor's day, Loki journeyed to the Cragmouth to speak with the Godstorm. He convinced the storm that Thor only wanted to enslave him. Loki also laid cunning spells on the Godstorm so that he could claim the storm's powers at any time. About a month later, Thor summoned the Godstorm to defeat a fleet of Berzerkir ships. Instead, the storm turned on Thor, knocking him out of the sky onto a Northmen ship. Thor retrieved his hammer and used its power to trap the Godstorm under the seafloor. Many centuries later, a man known as the Weather-Maker waited in prison for his day at court. He used a false tooth jammed with circuitry to summon the most violent storm it can find, and the Godstorm answered. The Godstorm empowered the supervillain, transforming him into Torrent. After Torrent and Thor battled, the God of Thunder used Mjolnir to transport Torrent to the Rock Troll fortifications. Odin stripped the Weather-Maker of his powers and sent him back to Earth. Some time later, an oil rig accidentally freed the Godstorm from his watery prison. Thor flew into the scene and ordered the storm to leave the oil rig workers unharmed and to prepare himself for battle. The Godstorm first struck at Mjolnir, causing Thor to fall into the sea. Thor sent the boulders from the seafloor at the Godstorm, who first laughed at Thor's mode of attacking before noticing the rocks still held confining magic. Nevertheless, the Godstorm stopped the attack and ensnared Thor. The God of Thunder tried to suffocate the storm by using Mjolnir, but the Godstorm returned the gesture by grabbing Thor and forcing him underwater. Loki watched the battle and sought to deliver the final blow against Thor. He attacked the Godstorm with a spell, causing the storm to lift Thor out of the water. Loki claimed the Godstorm's powers using the spells he had cast when they first met. As Thor battled Loki, the Godstorm realized he had been foolish for thinking himself mightier than the gods and mortals. He summoned his fellow storms of Cragmouth to defeat Loki.

fields.history: The Godstorm is the most powerful and violent storm in the world. After Loki's first unsuccessful attempt to summon a storm to ruin Thor's day, Loki journeyed to the Cragmouth to speak with the Godstorm. He convinced the storm that Thor only wanted to enslave him. Loki also laid cunning spells on the Godstorm so that he could claim the storm's powers at any time. About a month later, Thor summoned the Godstorm to defeat a fleet of Berzerkir ships. Instead, the storm turned on Thor, knocking him out of the sky onto a Northmen ship. Thor retrieved his hammer and used its power to trap the Godstorm under the seafloor. Many centuries later, a man known as the Weather-Maker waited in prison for his day at court. He used a false tooth jammed with circuitry to summon the most violent storm it can find, and the Godstorm answered. The Godstorm empowered the supervillain, transforming him into Torrent. After Torrent and Thor battled, the God of Thunder used Mjolnir to transport Torrent to the Rock Troll fortifications. Odin stripped the Weather-Maker of his powers and sent him back to Earth. Some time later, an oil rig accidentally freed the Godstorm from his watery prison. Thor flew into the scene and ordered the storm to leave the oil rig workers unharmed and to prepare himself for battle. The Godstorm first struck at Mjolnir, causing Thor to fall into the sea. Thor sent the boulders from the seafloor at the Godstorm, who first laughed at Thor's mode of attacking before noticing the rocks still held confining magic. Nevertheless, the Godstorm stopped the attack and ensnared Thor. The God of Thunder tried to suffocate the storm by using Mjolnir, but the Godstorm returned the gesture by grabbing Thor and forcing him underwater. Loki watched the battle and sought to deliver the final blow against Thor. He attacked the Godstorm with a spell, causing the storm to lift Thor out of the water. Loki claimed the Godstorm's powers using the spells he had cast when they first met. As Thor battled Loki, the Godstorm realized he had been foolish for thinking himself mightier than the gods and mortals. He summoned his fellow storms of Cragmouth to defeat Loki.

gojo.name: Gojo
gojo.origin: Professor Gojo was a spy for Imperial Japan that was active during World War II. By the summer of 1942, for unspecified reasons, he was considered a valued asset to American defense and was one of the few Japanese nationals living in the United States that was not confined to the internment camps. The American authorities were completely unaware that Gojo was a spy plotting an invasion of the Pacific Coast. In the interim, Gojo also trained other Japanese agents in the art of murder, and he took a perverse pleasure in keeping trophies of all his kills. thumb|left|Masked When an American spy learned of the location of the island where Gojo's planned invasion was located, he had the map tattooed on his scalp in an effort to smuggle the information out of Japan and back to the United States. When high ranking officials within Imperial Japan learned of this, they sent word to Gojo. Gojo tracked down the man and scalped him. The murder was witnessed by the Sub-Mariner who then attempted to stop Gojo. Gojo stabbed the Sub-Mariner in the shoulder with his knife and fled the scene. Because he was masked at the time of the murder, Gojo was the last suspect on the police's radar, who arrested famous Native American film star Johnny Feather-In-Hat as a suspect. The Sub-Mariner however was not convinced and using old fashioned detective work learned that Gojo was the man who purchased the knife he was stabbed with. The Sub-Mariner arrived at Gojo's home and confronted the spy in the middle of one of his murder training sessions. He learned the reason behind the murder and of the planned invasion. However, in attempting to apprehend Gojo, the Sub-Mariner was knocked out and shackled to a wall while the air raid began. Freeing himself, the Sub-Mariner confronted Gojo once again, who committed suicide due to the dishonor he felt for his foe breaking free. The Sub-Mariner soon used the scalp of Gojo's victim to track down the Japanese island base and with the aid of the Navy destroyed the island, ending the invasion.
weapons: Gojo was armed with various knives and bladed weapons.

gol goroth.name: Gol-Goroth
gol goroth.species: Dark god; Great or Lesser Old One
gol goroth.origin: ===Origins=== Gol-Goroth was either a Great or a Lesser Old One. ===Hyborian Age=== Gol-Goroth was the god of darkness in Bal-Sagoth. Kyrie, worshiped as sea-goddess Aala, once forbade the people to worship his image. She had her men to destroy it, in vain, so she bolted the doors of his temple. According to Kyrie, high priest of Bal-Sagoth and Gol-Goroth priest Gothan, after having exiled her, presumably reopened the temple and slew Aala's priests on its altars. ... Gol-Goroth was also invoked as part of invocations and spells: The sorcerer Costranno intended to sacrifice Berthilda the Brythunian to Gol-Goroth and Yog-Sothoth ("and all the fiends of the dark"), but was stopped by Conan and Red Sonja. His name was one of many invoked by Dharmi Shan .

Howard in his Conan story "The Gods of Bal-Sagoth" (1931, adapted by Marvel Comics in , August and September 1972), and incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos by Lin Carter. It is possibly the same being as Golgor, created by REH in his Solomon Kane story "The Moon of Skulls (first published in , June-July 1930; adapted in , 37 and 39, October, 1978, and February and April, 1979). Gol-Goroth's first reference in Marvel Comics was erroneously stated in the Demons' profile of the (September, 2007) to occur in (August, 1974) (where he was indeed referenced in the story "Curse of the Undead-Man"). The earliest reference occurred (August, 1972), while the first appearance occured in (September, 1972). In , he was mentioned as "Gol-Gorth", which was corrected in "Gol-Goroth" in the reprint in (August, 1976).

golden child moira vii 1.origin: thumb|left The unnamed baby dubbed "The Golden Child" by Mother Righteous was born to Wagnerine and Summernight, two Chimeras created by Mister Sinister, both with the DNA of Nightcrawler. Immediately after she was born, she began glowing gold and teleported to an unknown location. Her improbable, "miraculous" birth to two infertile Nightkin and subsequent disappearance were incorporated into Mother Righteous's religion. The personal tragedy, however, drove her father to suicide and her mother to turn against Righteous and her faith. Wagnerine soon discovered her daughter was the captive of the Mother and vowed to retrieve her. Nine hundred years later, Mother Righteous planned to use the child's soul as a sacrifice for her own ends. When Mister Sinister attempted to wipe out all mutant life to achieve Dominion, the reunited Wagnerine and/or her daughter were among the only three survivors.

golden skull.name: Golden Skull
golden skull.origin: The identity and true origin of the criminal known as the Golden Skull are a mystery. Some claimed he was the son of the environmental villain Green Skull, having rebelled against his father by becoming everything he hated. Others sustained that the Golden Skull was the nephew of the Plunderer, and inherited his uncle's obsession for material wealth and pirates. A theory even suggests the Golden Skull was a descendant of Revolutionary War fighter William Taurey. Regardless of the conflicting accounts of his origin, the Golden Skull's mission remained the same, to raze everything he could to soothe his warped ego. He doesn't think about anybody but himself, luring desperate people into working for him with false promises, and killing them once they stop being of use. thumb|left In the near future of 20XX, the Golden Skull was a recurring villain of Danielle Cage, the Captain America of that era. One of their numerous encounters happened when the villain took advantage of one instance of Manhattan's periodic flooding to steal several tanks of helium. The Skull and his henchmen were confronted by the hero. After his minions had been knocked out, and Captain America was getting ready to capture the Golden Skull, a mysterious rectangle of energy engulfed her (which was Time Platform). With the disappearance of Captain America, the Golden Skull resumed his objective, but he was soon knocked out by the returning hero, who had been delivered back to her time after an adventure in the future. She tied him up and brought him in his own boat to the rest of the Avengers. The Golden Skull would later set his sights on a particularly profitable target, an alternate timeline set in the past, where the catastrophic event that left his world in a state of ruin never happened. Together with his minions, the Golden Skull broke into the ruins of the Latverian Embassy, and got his hands on one of the world's last working time machines. Captain America tried to stop him, but failed. Once he arrived to the past, the Golden Skull used his knowledge from the future to seize the abandoned operations of the villain Arcade, turning the half-built All-In Casino into his base of operations. As part of a plan to seize control of the world's entire economy, the Golden Skull kidnapped wealthy CEO Bryce Wyne and replaced him with a robot duplicate. In turn, the robot duplicate arranged a gala at the Wyne International Hotel, where all attendants, some of the most influential millionaires in the globe, were abducted and replaced by robots. The Golden Skull was surprised by the arrival to the event of the U.S.Avegers, a group of heroes who had been tipped off about the Golden Skull's presence in their time by Captain America. The heroes' leader Bobby Da Costa had decided to attend the gala under the belief that its guests represented a target of opportunity for the Golden Skull. While da Costa's hunch proved right, the Golden Skull's potential targets had already become his victims. thumb|right|The Golden Skull's solid gold armor The Golden Skull had the duplicate robots attack the U.S.Avengers, but they failed to take down their target as the heroes had come prepared. When Iron Patriot analysed one of the robots and determined its origin as a creation of Arcade, Roberto had Captain America sweep the area for a potential location that could've served as one of Arcade's base, and the All-In Casino caught her attention, with further investigation confirming its origin as a front company for Arcade's operations. When Captain America broke into the All-In Casino, the Golden Skull re-calibrated Arcade's robot fabricators to maximum power, countering the hero with an army of robot pirates. Once the U.S.Avengers arrived to provide assistance, having finished dealing with the robot duplicates at the gala, Iron Patriot located the Golden Skull's control room and confronted him. In addition to having outfitted himself in a solid gold battle-suit, the villain threatened to use a trigger in his hand to boil alive the millionaires he had abducted, who were placed in stasis tubes in the room. After Enigma shot a laser that cut off the armor's hand that was holding the trigger, the Golden Skull attempted to confront the heroes directly. However, his splendor proved to be his fatal flaw. Iron Patriot effortlessly tore apart the Golden Skull's armor, due to gold being a soft metal and denting easily. After being secured, the Golden Skull was teleported back to his time with Captain America.

goldie centaurian.name: Goldie (Centaurian)
goldie centaurian.first_appearance: Silver Surfer: The Best Defense Vol 1 1
goldie centaurian.origin: Goldie was a Centaurian child living on a planet that had been pulled into The Train, an engine the size of a planetary system that consumed the planets on its path, stripping them of resources before using them to fuel its furnace. Goldie and her brothers were left by their father to fend for themselves. Together with her brothers, Goldie made a deal with another scavenger who would help them leave the planet in exchange for a device left by the Roxxon Corporation of Earth. When they came into conflict with Roxxon agents, all of Goldie's brothers were killed. Goldie managed to escape with the device, but the scavenger refused to follow through with the deal since Goldie and her brothers were supposed to deliver the artifact the previous night. A Roxxon agent killed the scavenger, dropping his body on top of Goldie, and escaped with the device to exchange it with Scrab Tongue for passage into his ship. After fending off two aliens that tried to steal her boots while she was immobilized by the scavenger's corpse, Goldie approached Scrab Tongue after he had turned down the Roxxon agent, and tried to reclaim the device with no success. Goldie then encountered the Silver Surfer, who was on a mission on the doomed planet to find a life worth sparing to convince Galactus not to find sustenance in the Train's planets. After the Silver Surfer defeated Scrab Tongue and his crewmen, and acquired the device, the Roxxon agent confronted him to reclaim the artifact. Goldie used her Yaka Arrows to kill the Roxxon agent, much to the Surfer's objection. Galactus determined no life on the planet was worth sparing, and prepared to consume it, but Goldie expressed no fear of him. The Surfer pointed Goldie to a vehicle left behind by Roxxon that she could use to escape from the planet before its destruction. Whether Goldie took Silver Surfer's advice and used the vehicle or not is unknown.

goldpool.name: Goldpool
goldpool.species: Golden clone of Deadpool and Masacre created through alchemy
goldpool.origin: Without a benefactor like the Grandmaster, M.O.D.O.K. struck up a deal with the Black-ISO Mafia in which he would create an army of unstoppable soldiers for them in exchange for help to keep his lab running. Intending to create golden clones of Deadpool through alchemy to compose said army, M.O.D.O.K. set up a lab in the Gold Realm, a section of Battlerealm abundant in gold, while members of the Black-ISO Mafia went after Deadpool. They, however, ended up capturing Masacre instead. Unaware that the copycat didn't have any of the powers the real Deadpool had, M.O.D.O.K. went on with the plan anyway. As he prepared the concoction for the creation of what would be the first of the golden soldiers, the Summoner invaded the Gold Realm with Deadpool, Domino, and the Avengers Unity Team to rescue Masacre. With time running short, M.O.D.O.K. threw Masacre inside the concoction. Deadpool tried to save Masacre, but ended up falling into the mixture as well, resulting in the creation of Goldpool, who had to be knocked out soon afterwards.

golem smoke elves.name: Golem (Smoke Elves)
golem smoke elves.origin: During the Fear, a couple of Smoke Elves assassins, worshipers of the Serpent, manipulated Tooth, a Dwarf of Nidavellir who had lost a fight against Tony Stark during his time in the Workshops of Svartalfheim and wanted revenge. As Stark was crafting weapons to oppose the Serpent, the Smoke Elves intended to kill him by fashioning a Golem out of mud. One of the Elves collected Stark's DNA using Tooth, before executing him. The golem was then released, attacking Stark during the night. As it was draining Stark, eating him alive, Splitlip (the ruler of the workshops) and his brethren attacked the golem (now shaped like Iron Man), giving the chance for Stark to destroy it and restore himself to full strength. The couple of Smoke Elves assassins were found by the Dwarves, and Splitlip stated they would be killed soon.

golem statue.name: Golem (Statue)
golem statue.origin: The Golem was an animated statue with superpowers created by Judah Loew ben Bezalel to protect the people of Prague. It was rediscovered in modern times and reanimated by archeologist Abraham Adamson as he lay dying and prayed for protection for his family against a group of army deserters. The Golem did indeed come to life, and slayed all of the deserters before returning to an inert state. Adamson's family then set sail with the Golem, to bring it to San Pedro University campus in Saint Petersburg, Florida. While en route, however, an evil wizard named Kaballa the Unclean learned of the Golem's discovery. Having searched for the statue himself for decades, Kaballa sent his air-demons to confront the Golem so he could capture it and use it in his plan for world domination. Despite the Golem's separation from land, the source of his powers, the Golem succeeded in fending off the demons, but not before they damaged their ship, causing it to sink. The Golem saved the Adamson family by swimming them to a nearby island. After being rescued, the Adamsons returned to San Pedro University with the Golem. Here Saudia Yamal confirmed the Golem to indeed be alive. Her supervisor, Professor Yeates, however, refused to accept this discovery after having spent years ridiculing Professor Adamson's belief in the rumours of the Golem. Worried that this would hurt his chances of inheriting Prof. Adamson's Department chairmanship, he attempted to destroy the Golem with a propane torch. When he turned it on though, it instead released Kaballa's fire-demons. The Golem instantly came to life again and fought with the demons, but fire is its natural weakness. It was able to overcome the demons, however, thanks to his emotional bond with the Adamson family whom he sought to protect. Sometime later, Kaballa separated the Golem from the Adamsons, weakening their bond and allowing Kaballa to take control of the statue. As a result, it went on a rampage in Saint Petersburg until he was opposed by the Thing who had just arrived in Florida on vacation with his girlfriend Alicia Masters. With the Adamsons help, the Golem was able to break free of Kaballa's control, forcing the evil wizard to flee. After which, the statue once again became inert.
powers: The Golem possesses and durability which can be amplified to unknown degrees when members of the Adamson family are in danger. It is impervious to bullets, explosions, and was able to stand toe-to-toe with the Thing.
weaknesses: Fire

goleta.name: Goleta
goleta.origin: Goleta was a barbarian warrior who despised magic and wandered Weirdworld slaughtering wizards for a living. When Becca the Earthgirl encountered Ogeode, the wizard was promptly killed by Goleta, which was witnessed by Warg, who notified the Witch Queen Le Fay that the the Wuxian Seed had fallen into Becca's possession. Alone in Weirdworld, Becca agreed to become Goleta's squire, and the two set off together, unknowingly being tracked by the Catbeast, which had emerged resurrected from Ogeode's corpse. While travelling around Weirdworld and training Becca to be her squire, Goleta was startled by the sudden appearance of the Catbeast and unintentionally drove off the road. There the pair were attacked by Sand Sharks and Becca was forced to operate Glorianna in order to rescue Goleta from the creatures. Upon reaching safety, the Catbeast revealed himself to be none other than Ogeode, forcing Becca to step between him and Goleta's axe, lest he be killed again before he could send her back to Earth. Ogeode then explained that in order to do so he needed to travel across the Fang Moutains to retrieve a spare wizard body, and offered to reveal the location of the Hidden Fortress of the Wilder Men in exchange for Goleta's help. The Wizardslayer agreed, only to discover they could not yet set out on this new adventure as, unfortunately due to her youth, Becca was not a very proficient driver, and had burned out the Glorianna's Emerald Fuel Injector during the escape from the Endless Desert. The trio went to see Nakia the Grand Mechanic, in order to barter for an Emerald Fuel Injector to repair the Glorianna, but she refused to help them because the Earthgirl's presence on Weirdworld unbalanced the fragile truce between the Swamp Queen Alliance and the Kingdom of the Torch. Having discovered Nakia spying on her, Morgan Le Fay unleashed the Mammoth Inferno, who led an assault on the Forge of the Grand Mechanic. During the ensuing chaos, Becca snuck off as Goleta and Ogeode watched the Giant Ghost Robot engage the Mammoth Inferno. Goleta then revealed that the reason she hated wizards was because she was from the Valley of the Burled Oak, a hamlet which was destroyed by the Wilder Men. Becca returned with a stolen Emerald Fuel Injector and the party fled to repair the Glorianna in order to continue with their quest.

golgor.name: Golgor
golgor.origin: ===Pre-Cataclysmic Age=== Golgor was a cruel god which worship replaced that of Valka in Negari, a colony planted by Atlantis during the Pre-Cataclysmic Age. ===Hyborian Age=== Negari and Golgor's worship persisted during the Hyborian Age, in the heart of Kush, though the city was ruled by blacks having overthrown the Atlanteans. ===16th century=== The worship kept on as Negari persisted, then in Africa.

gologolthia.origin: ===First Age of Monsters=== Gologolthia was originally an unnamed member of the Volantine Choir, a race of long-lived, winged creatures created according to the Above All's design, that lived in great sunlit forests, and beloved by Gaea. As Gaea did not undergo changes upon the arrival of the Mother of Horrors on Earth, the latter consequently visited the Volantine, blessing them with her corruptive seed, giving them claws and fangs, allowing them to also be diggers. The Volantine turn the forests barren, dug colonies of tunnels and burrow, and built from their own bones and viscera remarkable structures, making of their colony the first city on Earth. As the Volantine were slight and small, the Mother of Horrors chose one among them, blessed him with great size and strength, and commanded him to protect the Volantine and their city. She named him Gologolthia ("keeper of my children"). Gologolthia perched above the city, spreading his wings wide as the Volantine now favored shadow. As the monsters claimed dominion over Earth, the One Above All eventually took notice. He commanded Gaea and the Demiurge to mate, producing the Demogorge. ===Great Culling=== The Demogorge lay waste to the creations of the Mother of Horrors, consuming them one by one, until he came for the Volantine Choir. Gologolthia opposed him but was vastly outmached in a duel lasting a night and a day, during which his blood rained over the city. The Demorgoge finally struck him dead and he fell down. Meanwhile, the Volantine had fled underground, digging further than the Demorgoge could go despite breaking the Earth apart searching for them. Infuriated, the Demogorge rent Gologolthia's body apart, drenching the city in his blood until there was nothing left to desecrate. After the Demorgoge fled, the Volantine returned to their destroyed city. The Mother of Horrors' command to protect his kind wasn't lifted by Gologolthia's death. As his blood had seeped into the ground, stone and destroyed buildings, new towers of flesh rose from the Earth to replace the old structures. Thus, the Volantine survived the Great Culling, thanks to the sacrifice of Gologolthia. ===Later years=== Following the Great Culling, servants of One Above All returned many time to lay waste to the Living City, but every time it rose anew. It eventually came to host all of Vinruviel's children. Aeons later, circa 1600 BC, in Assyria, when Eldest sacked Nineveh and made it her capital, they summoned Gologolthia. The blood and spirit of Gologolthia imbued the stone of the city, watching over its monstrous dwellers. ===Modern Age / New Age of Monsters=== After taking control of the Hulk's persona body, Eldest came to Red Creek, Kentucky, where was set the Mountain Tomb of Udru, and summoned Gologolthia. Thus, Gologolthia became the sanctuary of the monsters in this new Age of Monsters, and her capital. ==Residents== Eldest / Hulk and her army: Udru Jinni Dagaal, the War Devil Skinwalkers Rutlings National Guard David Bridger Formerly: In Nineveh: Eldest / Child-God Charruk As the Living City of the Volantine Choir: Volantine Choir all of the Mother of Horrors' children

gomar.name: Gomar
gomar.origin: Gomar was a member of King Kull's Red Slayers, a group of the finest warriors of Valusia. Gomar and a group of Slayers accompanied Kull and Brule on their journey to find the fabled temple of the Serpent-Men. After being injured in an ambush by the Serpent-Men, Gomar was left behind while Kull led the healthy members of the group towards the temple. While the group was gone, Gomar was tended to and bandaged up. When Kull and company returned, they brought along Thulsa Doom, allegedly a man of Grondar found avenging his fiancé's death in the temple. Gomar immediately recognized Thulsa Doom and attempted to warn Kull, but at that moment, succumbed to his injuries, and fell off his horse to the ground, dead. Brule informed Kull he felt sorcery, and Thulsa Doom, responsible, but Kull dismissed the accusation for the time being.
abilities: As a Red Slayer, it can be assumed that Gomar was well-versed in combat.

gomurr.name: Gomurr
gomurr.species: Apprentice to an unnamed sorcerer, Gomurr and his rival Tar were responsible for sealing Cyttorak.
gomurr.origin: A group of monks sought to gain the power of Cyttorak, but were consumed by his destructive power. A tenuous alliance between the Ebon Vein and Gomurr's master led to the two combining their power. They managed to contain the essence in a crystal, which Cyttorak then cursed. Neither trusted the other in safeguarding the crystal, so a temple was chosen to house it. Years later, Cain Marko found the gem and was transformed into the Juggernaut. At some unknown point, Gomurr met Wolverine and the two became friends. Gomurr later migrated to the United States and worked out of a restaurant. When Psylocke was severely injured by Sabretooth, Archangel and Wolverine sought Gommur's help. He quickly determined that the Crimson Dawn would be able to heal her wounds. Doctor Strange noticed a magical disturbance and also arrived to lend his assistance. Tar was now the ruler of the Crimson Dawn and proctor of the Ebon Vein, but he was angry that Gomurr would make such a request. As the two continued their rivalry, Archangel was able to place a portion of Betsy's soul in the Dawn. Gomurr sensed Onslaught placing the Juggernaut into the Crimson Cosmos within the Ruby of Cyttorak. Doctor Strange also arrived at the Xavier Institute, and Gomurr asked Strange to guard the ruby while he entered the dimension. Tar also entered the ruby. Although the demoness Spite was able to trick Marko into confronting Cyttorak, the two sorcerers increased Juggernaut's powers so he could defeat the form Cyttorak took. Juggernaut was sent back to Earth, while Gomurr and Tar took refuge in the Crimson Dawn. When the villain Kuragari killed Tar and abducted Psylocke, Gomurr intervened and rescued her. Tar's spirit named Gomurr as his replacement as Proctor of the Crimson Dawn.

affiliations: Crimson Dawn (proctor) apparent long-time friend of Wolverine

Although the demoness Spite was able to trick Marko into confronting Cyttorak, the two sorcerers increased Juggernaut's powers so he could defeat the form Cyttorak took. Juggernaut was sent back to Earth, while Gomurr and Tar took refuge in the Crimson Dawn. When the villain Kuragari killed Tar and abducted Psylocke, Gomurr intervened and rescued her. Tar's spirit named Gomurr as his replacement as Proctor of the Crimson Dawn.

gondor.name: Gondor
gondor.origin: Gondor was a Nazi spy who was active during World War II. By 1942, his operations were operated out of the Gondor Funeral Home located in San Francisco. He would assist Japanese spies in smuggling themselves into the United States. To this end, he had them dispose of the bodies of American soldiers killed in the Pacific Theater and hide in their coffins. After the funerals of the deceased, the Japanese spies would be allowed free to commit acts of sabotage to American defense efforts. This plot was uncovered by the Angel who caught one of these spies attempting to signal the location where a new experiment jet was being developed by starting a fire. Using clues found on the man's body, the Angel followed them back to the Gondor funeral home. Finding the hero snooping around, Gondor had him ejected from the funeral home. Later, when the Angel returned, Gondor and his spies captured the hero and almost succeeded in having him buried alive at the funeral for a fallen soldier. Making enough noise to alert people to free him, the Angel took Gondor down, and he was promptly arrested by military authorities and locked up after he confessed his entire operation. Gondor's fate after the war is unrecorded.

gongniu.origin: Gōngniú was a member of Changdao's crew who was chosen to participate in a drinking challenge against the Invisible Woman. If Susan beat Gōngniú, Changdao would divulge the whereabouts of S.H.I.E.L.D. Agent Aidan Tintreach to them. After nine rounds of whiskey shots, Susan beat Gōngniú as he passed out on the floor in a drunken stupor. But it was revealed that Changdao poisoned Gōngniú's drinks thus killing him while he called on his bodyguards to do the same thing to the women.

gonji.name: Gonji
gonji.origin: thumb|left|125px|Ganji the medicine man Gonji was a medicine man for an unknown Native American tribe that operated out of a southern state that even by the 1941's still remained true to their heritage. His tribe worshiped the wolf, and when they discovered gold on their land and began mining it, the greedy Gonji used local superstition to trick his fellow people into giving him large amounts of gold. To this end, he constructed a convincing wolf costume and posed as the "Wolf-That-Walked-Like-A-Man", attacking his own people until they began providing gold offerings to appease the angry "God". The series of murders attracted the attention of the hero known as the Angel who was not convinced that these killings were the work of a Wolf-Man. Witnessing an offering, the Angel waited until the so-called Wolf-Man came to collect the gold and chased after it. Gonji had trained normal wolves to do his bidding, and they kept the Angel at bay long enough for his fellow tribesmen to capture the Angel and tie him up to a totem pole in sacrifice. When the Wolf-Man attempted to attack the Angel, the hero broke free and fought the "beast" into fleeing back to his cave. There, the Angel beat the Wolf-Man into submission, unmasking him and revealing his true identity and motives. The Angel then turned Gonji over to his people to face justice, and he was summarily executed for his crimes.
weapons: Gonji wore a lifelike wolf costume that has razor sharp claws and teeth. He had trained wolves to follow his command and attack his opponents.

gonra.name: Gonra
gonra.origin: thumb|left|350px|Gonra fighting off hordes of Atlanteans before the Temple of the Scorpion|Temple of the Scorpion God ===19,500 BC=== Circa 19,500 BC, one thousand years before the Age of Kull, Gonra of the Sword was an ancient Valusian hero and knight, who had slain thousands of opponents, and bested the greatest warriors of his age. Gonra wielded a sword forged by a priest or a sorcerer, and fired upon by fire of Heaven and by Valusia's Scorpion God himself. He battled hordes of savage Atlanteans when they had decided to destroy Valusia's Scorpion God. That day, Gonra eventually fell to the Atlanteans but saved the Temple of the Scorpion and Valusia as a whole. He was buried in armor in a sepulchre in the woods beside the temple, but his sword was hidden away. ===18,500 BC=== As Count Murom Bora Ballin's daughter Daphna wished to have King Kull love her, she visited the Sorceress, who found out in her Moon-Gem that Kull's favor could be won by finding him a champion that was his equal, as Brule had left Kull and had returned to the Pictish Isles. After she informed Kull, he went with the poet Ridondo to the temple of the Scorpion, retrieved the sword, and finally freed Gonra from his tomb of vines, and defeated him in combat, forcing him to yield before declaring Gonra his equal. The conspirators Meicus and Duarvio intended to plunder the Accursed Room, the throneroom where King Eallal had been murdered by Snake-Men, for riches, despite Meicus' concern about the curse. They taunted a drunken Gonra into opening the door, sealed by Kull who had sank a sword into the lock. Once the Room open, Meicus was frightened to death by the ghost of Eallal, and Gonra slew many Snake-Men before retreating, wounded, to warn Kull, who had already taken the path to the Accursed Room and defeated many Snake-Men himself, including an impersonator of Gonra. Kull decided to cleansed with fire and seal with brick and mortar the Accursed Room. Gonra eventually left and Brule returned, in adventures yet to be recounted.
abilities: Gonra was a formidable warrior thousands of opponents, and bested the greatest warriors of his age. A thousand years later, he was bested by Kull, who considered him his equal.
